guide.h: Two ways to describe a change

guide.p: You can use a verb with an adverb, or an adjective with a noun. Mixing both patterns gives your writing variety.

guide.example: Verb + adverb: 'Sales rose sharply in 2015.'  Adjective + noun: 'There was a sharp rise in sales in 2015.'

bullets: rose to 40% — the final value
rose by 10% — the size of the change
a rise of 10% — the size of the change (noun)
a rise in sales — what changed (noun)
stood at / was at 30% — a value at one point
peaked at 75% — the highest point
from 20% to 35% — start and end values
Big changes: soar, rocket, surge, plummet, plunge; dramatically, sharply, significantly.
Medium changes: rise, increase, fall, decline; considerably, steadily, noticeably.
Small changes: dip, edge up; slightly, marginally, gradually.
No change: remain stable, remain steady, level off, plateau, stay constant.
Up and down: fluctuate, be volatile.

guide.tip: Use strong verbs only when the data really shows a dramatic change. 'Soared' for a 2% rise is inaccurate and is marked down.

bullets: X was higher than Y. / X was the highest of all.
X was twice / three times as high as Y.
X was almost double the figure for Y.
X accounted for / made up / represented 40% of the total.
X rose, whereas / while Y fell.
By contrast, … / In comparison, … / Similarly, …
The same was true of …
X and Y followed similar patterns.
just over / slightly more than 50%
just under / nearly / almost 50%
approximately / roughly / around 50%
about a quarter / a third / half / two thirds / three quarters
the vast majority / a small minority
over the period / throughout the period
between 2000 and 2010
in the following decade
by 2020 (= at or before 2020 — often with past perfect: 'By 2020 the figure had doubled')
from then on / after that / at the end of the period

vocab.meaning: to go up
vocab.example: The number of cyclists rose by 15% over the decade.

vocab.meaning: to go up gradually, often over a long time
vocab.example: Prices climbed steadily throughout the 1990s.

vocab.meaning: to rise very quickly to a high level
vocab.example: Online sales soared after 2019.

vocab.meaning: a sudden large increase (noun or verb)
vocab.example: There was a surge in demand for bicycles in 2020.

vocab.meaning: to go down
vocab.example: Coal use declined steadily between 1990 and 2020.

vocab.meaning: to fall, often quickly
vocab.example: Attendance dropped to 40% in the final year.

vocab.meaning: to fall very quickly and by a lot
vocab.example: Profits plummeted from $8 million to $1 million.

vocab.meaning: a small, temporary fall
vocab.example: Sales dipped slightly in 2014 before recovering.

vocab.meaning: to go up and down irregularly
vocab.example: The temperature fluctuated between 18 and 24 degrees.

vocab.meaning: to stop rising or falling and stay at a similar level
vocab.example: Membership levelled off at around 5,000.

vocab.meaning: to stay the same
vocab.example: The figure for rail travel remained stable at 12%.

vocab.meaning: to reach the highest point
vocab.example: Visitor numbers peaked at 2.4 million in 2018.

vocab.meaning: to reach the lowest point before rising again
vocab.example: Unemployment bottomed out at 4% in 2019.

vocab.meaning: to rise again after a fall
vocab.example: Tourism recovered quickly after 2021.

vocab.meaning: to become higher than something that was higher before
vocab.example: Laptops overtook desktops in 2014.

vocab.meaning: by a large amount, quickly
vocab.example: Water use increased sharply in summer.

vocab.meaning: by a large amount
vocab.example: The cost of housing rose considerably.

vocab.meaning: at a regular, even rate
vocab.example: The population grew steadily over the century.

vocab.meaning: by a small amount
vocab.example: The figure fell marginally, from 51% to 49%.

vocab.meaning: to form a part or percentage of a total
vocab.example: Wind power accounted for a quarter of all electricity.

vocab.meaning: used to contrast two facts in one sentence
vocab.example: Car use rose, whereas bus use fell.

vocab.meaning: two times the size or amount
vocab.example: Men were twice as likely as women to cycle to work.

vocab.meaning: more than half
vocab.example: The majority of students lived on campus.

vocab.meaning: in the same order as the things just mentioned
vocab.example: France and Spain received 30% and 25% respectively.

vocab.meaning: close to but not exactly
vocab.example: Approximately 60% of homes had a garden.

vocab.meaning: the number or percentage belonging to something
vocab.example: The figure for Japan was much lower.
